newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc to raise payout ratio.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc to raise payout ratio.

text.p: PARIS, Jan 30 - Rhone-Poulenc chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou told a news conference that the company planned to have a 45 percent dividend payout ratio against 41 percent in 1996.
He said that the integration of British company Fisons Plc was going well and would generate synergy benefits of more than $200 million.
Fisons has been acquired by Rhone-Poulenc's 68 percent unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
"Fisons has been neutral for 1996, there was a negative effect in the first half and a positive effect in the second half," Fourtou told a news conference on the 1996 results.
He said that at the end of 1996 Rhone-Poulenc had total divestments of 6.8 billion francs.
"We said that we would sell 10 billion francs in two-years, in 1997 we will exceed this number," he said.
Fourtou said the company's 1996 net income rose by 28.4 percent.
"This is an encouraging figure, but it remains insufficient for a company of our size," he said

He said there were three negative elements in the group's results -- the recall at Centeon, a crisis in polyester, which reduced operating income by 700 million francs, and the very low price of titanium dioxide.
